bluf: Uplix is a founder led Paris agency, founded in 2020 by Emmanuel de Vauxmoret, selling SEO and GEO first, with search ads, social ads and data tracking in the core. The record shows it pushing into AI answers and assistant ads, with a guide to the August 2026 ChatGPT Ads launch in France and 577 AI topic URLs in its sitemap, but no dated moves, news or open roles. Its book holds 9 clients, 0 observed and 9 names only, against a claim of 200+ brands. A rival should know its own house practises 0 of the 3 lines the Radar could test.
doing:
Uplix sells search first, then media and data, to French brands. Its positioning line, a Paris SEO, media and data agency steering brands' digital growth with tailored, performance led strategies run by experts and proprietary technology, means: rankings first, then search and social ads and tracking, run by its own people and tools. The headline claim is scale and one rank: growth sped up for 200+ brands, with MAAF ranking first for 'assurance auto'. Founded in 2020 and led by its founder, Emmanuel de Vauxmoret, it lists one office, in the 8th arrondissement of Paris, and no headcount.

The sold mix leads with SEO and AI Search / GEO, both scored 3: the title and homepage lead with Agence SEO, the SEO menu spans audit, content, migration and netlinking, and the markup bills it a GEO/IA agency with GEO as a top level menu. Paid Search, Paid Social and Data & Measurement score 2: a MEDIA menu with Google and Microsoft Ads pages, an SMA menu with Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn and YouTube Ads pages, and a DATA menu for data SEO, dashboarding and tracking. AI Automation, CRO and Content & Digital PR score 1 without notes. The positioning claims proprietary technology and the GEO page cites in house R&D tools, yet the record names no proprietary product and no partner.

Its AI posture is commercial: GEO for presence in ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini answers, AI process automation, and coverage of ChatGPT Ads, including the guide to their August 2026 launch in France. The Horus read has it making P8, ads inside assistants tested with holdouts. The record lists no dated moves, no news and no pricing signal, and its applicant tracking page on wttj shows 0 jobs. The dated items are sector pages: Secteurs (2024-10-03); Food, Santé and Retail (2024-11-17); banking and insurance (2025-10-24). Conspicuously absent for an agency claiming 200+ brands: a single case study that describes the work.
clients:
The client type is mixed, across banking and insurance, luxury, services, health, retail, fashion, travel and tourism, and education, sold from one Paris office. The needs read holds 9 clients, 0 observed and 9 names only: every name comes from a client slug page that yielded no signal, so the need mix is empty and every need below is inferred.

The claims give some of them a direction. The headline credits MAAF with ranking first for 'assurance auto', and the cases page claims rank wins for MAAF, Acadomia, K-Way and La Maison Convertible, so organic demand is the likely need for those brands (moderate confidence), though the read codes them names only; K-Way sits on record as K-Way France. Orange Money, Courchevel, Gandi, Sushi Shop and Sonia Rykiel carry nothing but the slug: their need is inferred from what Uplix leads with, SEO and GEO, with search and social ads the likely second line (low confidence).

The sector pages, dated 2024-10-03 to 2025-10-24, carry navigation text rather than described work, so they add no need signal. No client is shared with another tracked agency, and none carries a date, so the record cannot say which accounts are current.

Under KJ1 (the click replaced by the citation) it is likely, moderate confidence, that the rank win brands will next need proof of presence in AI answers, which Uplix sells; under KJ2 (ads inside AI answers) its ChatGPT Ads coverage makes assistant ad tests the likely next line it sells them (low confidence).

market:
The Horus read puts Uplix at a tailwind index of 14.6, band Favored, percentile 59. It is best placed for KJ1 (the click replaced by the citation) and KJ2, both driven by AI Search / GEO and Paid Search, and most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle hollowed out), driven by SEO, Paid Search and Paid Social, and KJ4 (platforms absorbing execution), driven by the two paid lines. Best scenario fit: The Bazaar of Agents at 47/100. It is making P4 and P8, partial on P1, absent on P2, P6 and P7, unknown on P5; P3 does not apply.

The Monsoon read is 57.7, band Onshore wind: migration 56.2 against displacement 59.2. The sold mix supplies 56 of the index, SEO (18) and AI Search / GEO (9) carrying the most movable hours, 23% of which automation overlaps; the work would go 45% to Africa and the Maghreb, 30% to South and Southeast Asia and 20% to Eastern Europe. No hub office is listed; the footprint is inferred. Its onshore claim concerns in house R&D tools, not where people sit.
openings:
The strongest opening is the say and do record, 0 of 3 tested lines practised. Uplix sells paid social on Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn and YouTube with no social ad pixel on its own site, sells LinkedIn ads with 0 of its own, and sells GEO with no llms.txt. It is likely, moderate confidence, that a rival showing its own live social and LinkedIn programmes wins a side by side pitch for paid social budgets. The book is thin in public: 9 of 9 clients names only against a claim of 200+ brands, so every account is contestable on proof, Orange Money, Courchevel, Gandi, Sushi Shop and Sonia Rykiel most of all, since no claim attaches to them (low confidence). The record shows no feed, schema or entity work (P2 absent) and no audited AI visibility product (P1 partial), so a rival reporting citation share leads with the number, and an outcome priced offer meets a firm with no public pricing (P5 unknown). A rival should not lead on ChatGPT Ads, where Uplix is making P8.
